rules.title: Money sent abroad over 12 months
rules.question: Could the money you've logged as sent abroad in the last 12 months add up to a figure some countries ask people to report?
rules.match_description: transactions whose title, store or notes mention a remittance, a wire or money transfer, Wise, Western Union, MoneyGram or 송금
rules.assumption_statement: Meika assumes a figure of USD 10,000 sent abroad within 12 months.
rules.verification_prompt: Ask a tax professional where you live whether any reporting rule applies to money you send abroad, and at what amount.
rules.source_note: USD 10,000 appears as a reporting figure in several countries' rules, which is the only reason it is used here as a placeholder. Meika does not know whether it applies to you.

rules.title: One large transfer abroad
rules.question: Is any single transfer abroad you've logged large enough that it might be worth asking about?
rules.match_description: transactions whose title, store or notes mention a remittance, a wire or money transfer, Wise, Western Union, MoneyGram or 송금
rules.assumption_statement: Meika assumes a figure of USD 3,000 for a single transfer.
rules.verification_prompt: Ask a tax professional whether a single large transfer abroad needs any paperwork where you live.
rules.source_note: USD 3,000 is a round cut-off with no external basis. It is only here so one unusually large transfer gets a second look.

rules.title: Education and housing costs with no receipt recorded
rules.question: Are you building up education or housing costs this tax year without a receipt recorded for them?
rules.match_description: Education or Housing & Utilities expenses in this tax year that you haven't marked as having a receipt
rules.assumption_statement: Meika assumes ₩1,000,000 of such costs without a receipt is worth a look.
rules.verification_prompt: Ask a tax professional whether any of these costs could matter for your return, and which records you would need to keep.
rules.source_note: ₩1,000,000 is a round cut-off with no external basis. Some countries let people claim education or housing costs; whether yours does, and which records it asks for, Meika does not know.

rules.title: Education spending this tax year
rules.question: Could your education spending this tax year reach a level where it's worth asking how it's treated?
rules.match_description: Education expenses in this tax year
rules.assumption_statement: Meika assumes ₩5,000,000 of education spending in one tax year is worth a question.
rules.verification_prompt: Ask a tax professional whether education costs are treated in any special way where you file.
rules.source_note: ₩5,000,000 is a round cut-off with no external basis.

rules.title: Spending in several currencies
rules.question: Does your spending in several currencies over the past year form a pattern worth mentioning to an adviser?
rules.match_description: expenses logged in a currency other than KRW
rules.assumption_statement: Meika treats spending in 2 or more foreign currencies, making up at least 25% of your spending, across at least 3 months, as a pattern.
rules.verification_prompt: Ask a tax professional whether spending in several countries says anything about where you are treated as resident. That usually depends on days present, which Meika cannot see.
rules.source_note: These cut-offs are arbitrary: 2 is the smallest number that makes 'several currencies' true, 3 months separates a holiday from a pattern, and 25% has no external basis.

rules.title: Regular payments that run past the tax year end
rules.question: Do any of your regular payments continue past the end of this tax year, so part of the cost lands in the next one?
rules.match_description: still-active payments that repeat at least 3 times at a regular interval (grouped by category and exact store or title)
rules.assumption_statement: Meika treats regular payments worth ₩1,200,000 or more a year as worth mentioning.
rules.verification_prompt: Ask a tax professional whether it matters which tax year a regular payment falls in.
rules.source_note: ₩1,200,000 a year (₩100,000 a month) is a round cut-off with no external basis. Meika sees payment dates, not what period each payment covers.
